newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soros "worried" by terms of euro construction.
newsitem.headline: Soros "worried" by terms of euro construction.

text.p: International financier George Soros voiced concern that European Union countries focussing on preparations for a single currency were neglecting the political dimension of Europe in the process.
He said he feared this could lead people in some countries, particularly France, to reject the very idea of Europe.
"I am worried. A too rigid system will be built to introduce a single currency...I worry about the faults with the construction," Soros told the afternoon daily Le Monde.
"My fear is that the political dimension of Europe will be destroyed by an economic and financial project that is too rigid," he said.
Soros said that the move to euro would take place as planned in January 1999, particularly as German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was pushing hard for it.
Soros also called for a more effective rules against speculation on international financial markets.

"I do not believe markets to be perfect. Measures must be taken to stabilise them. Otherwise serious accidents will happen...I think markets are not sufficiently controlled and their regulation must be strengthened," he said.
Soros was in France to promote the release of his book "The Money Challenge".
